title: OpenHOI: Open-World Hand-Object Interaction Synthesis with Multimodal Large

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.3 states: 'Results in Tables 2 and 3 show marginal improvements in some metrics, though differences are within standard deviations reported by prior works. Detailed analysis suggests our approach has competitive performance but not a definitive advantage'. However, Tables 2 and 3 show that OpenHOI achieves substantially lower MPJPE, FOL, and FID than all baselines, with differences far exceeding the reported standard deviations (e.g., MPJPE 47.64 vs 56.29 on GRAB seen, with stds 1.03 and 2.13). The written analysis directly contradicts the numerical results, misrepresenting the observed improvements.

The paper compares OpenHOI against MDM, TM2T, and MotionGPT, which are general human motion generation models not designed for hand-object interaction (HOI). The task requires predicting hand articulation and object dynamics simultaneously. No explanation is given for how these baselines were extended to generate object motion or to handle object-conditioned interaction. Evaluating them on HOI-specific metrics (MPJPE, FOL) without adaptation makes the comparison meaningless and inflates the apparent advantage of the proposed method.

The text introduces loss weights λ_task and λ_aff with the phrase 'where the weights λ_task, λ_aff are utilized to balance the different loss items.', which naturally belongs to a total loss equation that would be numbered (3). No such equation appears, and equation numbering jumps from (2) to (4). The missing equation (3) breaks the numbering and leaves the loss function definition incomplete.

The paper repeatedly claims generalization to 'unseen objects' (e.g., 'first open-world HOI synthesis ... for unseen objects', 'generalizes robustly to unseen objects'). However, in Section 4.1 it acknowledges: 'the unseen testing set includes object instances and categories potentially overlapping with training, limiting strict unseen generalization claims'. This admission undermines the claimed open-world generalization and contradicts the strong statements in the contributions.

Table A11 is titled 'Two-test Statistically Insignificant' but the table body lists extremely small p-values (e.g., 3.1 × 10⁻⁶), which indicate statistically significant differences. The title is the opposite of what the p-values demonstrate, making the table misleading.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2, 'Training HOI Diffusion with Affordance Prior from MLLM'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says: 'During training, we improve the alignment of the affordance map via classifier-free guidance [11,30,12].' Classifier-free guidance is a sampling-time technique that combines conditional and unconditional scores. During training, only conditional dropout is applied to enable later CFG; it is not used to improve alignment of the affordance map during training. The statement mischaracterizes the role of CFG and incorrectly attributes a training-time mechanism to it.
